overview.description: Bridge with Semi-Exposed Dummies (also known as Honeymoon Bridge variant) is a two-player adaptation of Contract Bridge. It solves the issue of missing players by using two 'Semi-Exposed' hands on the table. Each dummy consists of stacks of cards where only the top card is visible. As cards are played, the hidden cards underneath are revealed. This creates a strategic duel where players must manage their own hand while navigating the unknown elements of the table dummies.

history.origins: Developed as a 'Honeymoon' Bridge variant to allow two players to enjoy the strategic complexity of Bridge without a full table. It borrows the 'uncovering' mechanic from games like German Whist.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Honeymoon Bridge variants proliferate.
1950s: The semi-exposed dummy format becomes a standard recommendation in Bridge primers for two players.
Present: Popular as a training tool for Bridge players to practice card-reading and deduction.
history.evolution: The game shifted from simple 'Draw Whist' to this format to better simulate the presence of four hands and the partnership dynamics of standard Bridge.
history.cultural: A staple of the 'Honeymoon' card game sub-genre, emphasizing intimacy and mental rivalry.

setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 cards in hand. Two dummy hands of 13 cards each are dealt to the table in stacks: 6 face-down cards each covered by a face-up card, with one extra face-up card.

rules.objective: Win enough tricks to fulfill the contract, using both your hand and your designated dummy hand.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Auction**: Players bid for trumps as in standard Bridge. 2. **Play**: Each turn involves playing two cards—one from the player's hand and one from their dummy. 3. **Uncovering**: When a face-up dummy card is played, the face-down card beneath it is flipped over and becomes available for the next trick.
keyRules: Must follow suit from the specific source hand (Player Hand or Dummy Hand).
The highest card among the four cards played wins the trick for the team.
Standard Bridge bidding and scoring applies.

strategy.basic: Identify the high cards in the dummies early. Use your hand to support your dummy's weak suits and vice-versa.
strategy.intermediate: Deduction: Since you see your hand and the top cards of both dummies, you can calculate the probabilities of hidden cards in the face-down stacks vs. the opponent's hand.
strategy.advanced: Endplay setup: Force the opponent to uncover their dummy cards in a specific order, potentially trapping their high cards under your own established winners.
tips: Don't uncover cards too fast if your hand is weak; you might reveal a high card your opponent can easily capture.
Save your hand's trumps to protect your dummy's high side-suit cards.

list.name: Full Exposed Dummy
list.description: All 13 cards of the dummies are dealt face-up immediately, making it a game of perfect information.
list.emptyOverridesReason: This variation only changes how visible the dummy cards are; the underlying engine phases and actions remain the same.

difficulty.easy: Plays dummy cards randomly. Does not attempt to deduce face-down cards.
difficulty.medium: Tracks played cards. Understands simple finessing using the dummy upcards.
difficulty.hard: Optimal Bayesian deduction. Calculates the exact probability of every hidden card location. Uses Minimax to optimize the 26-card combined team play.

considerations: Must manage four distinct card sources (2 hands, 2 dummies).
Requires logic for handling the 'Uncover' event as a state-change trigger.

ante.reason: This game is a point-based Bridge variant and does not utilize a monetary or chip-based ante system.

deal.reason: The complex distribution of hand cards and semi-exposed dummy cards is performed automatically by the system.

reveal_market.reason: This is a closed-hand game where only the dummy top cards are public; no shared community market exists.

buy_market.reason: Players cannot purchase or swap cards from any external area; they must succeed with their dealt cards.

buy_stock.reason: The entire 52-card deck is distributed at the start; no cards remain in stock to be drawn during play.

fold.reason: Both players are committed to playing out all 13 tricks to determine the final point winner of the deal.

check.reason: The game uses a trick-taking and bidding structure rather than a vying structure where checking would apply.

call.reason: There is no pot or bet to match in this game; competition is based strictly on contract point accumulation.

bet.reason: Success is determined by trick wins and bidding precision rather than through financial or chip-based betting.

raise.reason: Bids are escalated during the auction phase via bidding rather than through wagering rounds during play.

declare.reason: Hand strength is established during the showdown comparison rather than through a formal declaration phase.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands stay private until cards are played into tricks; dummy top cards are already public information.

award_pot.reason: Winning points are added to a cumulative partnership total rather than awarded from a physical pot.

play_card.description: Play a card from either the private hand or the designated dummy stack.
play_card.constraints: Must follow suit; highest card of led suit or highest trump wins.

draw.reason: Each player receives their complete set of cards at the start; no drawing phase exists during play.

discard.reason: Every card in the hand and dummy must be played into a trick; no cards are discarded or buried.

pass.description: Pass during the auction when choosing not to bid a higher contract.

bid.description: Place a bid for a contract consisting of a trick count and a suit choice.
bid.constraints: Must exceed the current high bid in rank or level.

meld.reason: This is strictly a trick-taking game based on card values rather than forming sequences or melds.

go_out.reason: The hand terminates automatically once all thirteen tricks have been played by both participants.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: The hand and dummy sizes are fixed at 13; no draw pile exists during the trick-taking play.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Cards are played directly to tricks; no separate waste or discard pile is utilized.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Cards contribute only their rank and suit values to tricks; no card has a secondary engine action.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: Bidding results are public between the two players; no hidden tokens are required.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: This is a trick-taking game and does not use a capture-from-tableau fishing mechanic.
notApplicableReasons.meldConfig: Points are earned strictly through trick counting; no melding of card sets is part of the gameplay.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: This game is not a shedding game; players maintain their hands throughout the deal.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: None; highest card of lead suit or highest trump wins the trick.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Highest bidder leads first trick; thereafter trick winner leads.

customActions.description: Distribute 13 hand cards and 13 dummy cards to each player.
Select a card from the private hand to play to the trick.
Select an available face-up dummy card to play to the trick.
Bid the contract level and trump suit (or no-trump).
Calculate match points based on contract and tricks made.
customActions.constraints: System automatic scoring at hand end.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; card rank comparison determines trick winner (Ace is high).
engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. No jokers; used for bridge with semi-exposed dummies where part of the dummy is visible during the auction or play.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Suit hierarchy for bidding is spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs, then no-trump. Follow suit when possible; declarer plays from hand and dummy (semi-exposed as per variant).
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit in standard order: ace, king, queen, jack, ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two. Trick order is standard; the contract is determined by the auction and the dummy is partially exposed.
engine.dealPattern: Cards dealt to hands and then to stacked table dummies.

hero.title: HONEYMOON BRIDGE
hero.subtitle: Semi-Exposed Dummy Variant
hero.tagline: Two players. Four hands. One strategic duel.

synthesis.shortDescription: The perfect solution for two Bridge enthusiasts. Manage your own hand while controlling a stacked dummy on the table. Every card played from the dummy reveals a hidden layer of strategy, making this variant a high-skill duel of memory and deduction.

prompts.human: Your dummy has the Ace of Spades face-up, covering a hidden card. Should you play it now to win the lead, or keep it to trap the opponent's King later?
prompts.ai: Game: Bridge with Semi-Exposed Dummies. Type: 2-Player Bridge. Rules: 13 cards in hand + 13 in stacked table dummy per player. Auction sets contract. Play involves hand and dummy cards. Uncovering hidden cards adds variance.

scoring.description: Standard Bridge scoring with two-player adjustments.
scoring.winCondition: Fulfill the contract or reach target match score.

penalties.Undertricks: Opponent scores points for every trick failed by the declarer.

scoring.splitRules: None; only one player can win the deal or match.

nullReasons.targetScore: Reaching 100 points 'Below the Line' constitutes one game.
nullReasons.cardValues: Individual cards contribute to trick wins rather than having point values.
